cases.title: Chinese farm machinery for flood-hit households sold on instead of handed out
cases.place: Zenica-Doboj, Tuzla and Posavina cantons, Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina
cases.point: Sarajevo, seat of the Federation government whose commission allocated the machinery; the households it was meant for are in the Zenica-Doboj, Tuzla and Posavina cantons (Nominatim for Sarajevo; cantons from AidData record 66093)

lenders.name: Government of China
lenders.role: Grant agreement signed in 2014 with the Government of Bosnia and Herzegovina for agricultural machinery worth about 1 million convertible marks, around half a million euros; the machinery arrived in the summer of 2014 and was handed over on 23 July 2014, earmarked for the flood-hit Zenica-Doboj, Tuzla, Posavina and Brčko districts (AidData record 66093). Radio Free Europe gives the wider Chinese donation of farm equipment to Bosnia and Herzegovina, intended for returnees, at more than six million convertible marks, a third of which the Council of Ministers directed to the Federation government after the floods of May 2014.

cases.conditions: The aid was Chinese-made equipment rather than money. The Indirect Taxation Authority of Bosnia and Herzegovina supervised its distribution (AidData record 66093). The Federation government set up a commission to allocate its share against fixed criteria: a registered farm, flood damage verified by the municipal authority, and no earlier donation of the same kind (Radio Free Europe).

companies.name: Government of the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina
companies.role: Took delivery of the Federation's share and appointed the commission that was to allocate it; the commission was chaired by Ivica Mladina, then an adviser to Federation prime minister Nermin Nikšić (Radio Free Europe)
companies.desc: The executive of the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina, one of the country's two entities. Its agriculture, water management and forestry ministry handles farm support, and for this donation the government formed a separate allocation commission of government advisers and officials.

cases.community: The Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina was allocated 96 tractors with attachments, 37 motocultivators, 52 chainsaws, 26 milking sets, 22 milk coolers and 11 milk analysers (Radio Free Europe). Police detained eight people in an operation code-named Farmer, and on 2 April 2019 arrested Desnica Radivojević, a former Federation minister and deputy prime minister, in Sarajevo (index.hr; Radio Free Europe). A cantonal court ordered one month in custody for Ivica Mladina, who chaired the allocation commission, and for Refik Džafo and Vahid Jašarević; the other five detainees were released under restrictions. Police seized 28 tractors and farm machines that had been sold and handed to third parties. The prosecution says the suspects found buyers, or fictitious recipients recorded on paper as receiving equipment that was then sold on; that Mladina offered tractors for 10,000 to 15,000 convertible marks each; and that the group's unlawful gain exceeded one million marks (prosecutors Nevena Alićehajić and Željka Tomić-Anđušić, quoted by Radio Free Europe). The prosecution also says that from 2015, after his government post ended, Mladina took 2,000 to 5,000 marks, and in one case 20,000, from people he promised to arrange a tractor for, presenting himself as a government commissioner or as a consultant to the Chinese embassy, and that he deceived more than 50 people this way. index.hr puts the value of the equipment in the resale case at about 500,000 euros. The Chinese embassy in Sarajevo said it had learned from the media that the donated equipment had been sold, and that it had not been handed to the residents hit by the floods (Radio Free Europe).
cases.displaced_note: No count of people was published. The flood-hit households the machinery was meant for are named by canton and not counted in any document read.
cases.outcome: Four men were in custody in April 2019 and the case sat with the Sarajevo Cantonal Prosecutor's Office. Nermin Nikšić, prime minister at the time of the allocation, said the commission had been formed to make the process transparent and that Mladina should answer if the accusations were true (Radio Free Europe).

sources.publisher: Radio Free Europe / Radio Slobodna Evropa

sources.title: Uhićen bivši ministar iz BiH. Krao je od donacija za poplave?
Chinese Government provides grant for provision of agricultural machinery (record 66093)

cases.confidence_note: Two independent outlets carry the arrests, the seizure of 28 machines and the prosecution's figures, and the Chinese embassy confirmed the equipment did not reach flood-hit residents. The sale itself, the one-million-mark gain and the more than 50 people defrauded are the prosecution's case, not a court finding; no verdict has been reported in the sources read. The dates of the donation differ inside one article: its opening says China gave the tractors in 2012, while the prosecutor quoted lower down says China donated in 2014, which is also the year AidData gives for the grant agreement. No document counts the households that went without.
cases.whole: The wider Chinese donation of farm equipment to Bosnia and Herzegovina was worth more than six million convertible marks and was meant for returnees; AidData's record puts the 2014 grant agreement at about one million marks, around half a million euros. The Federation's share came to 96 tractors with attachments, 37 motocultivators, 52 chainsaws, 26 milking sets, 22 milk coolers and 11 milk analysers. Police recovered 28 of the machines in 2019.

cases.title: Route 32 widening: land put to work before the expropriation payments were settled
cases.place: National Route 32, Route 4 junction to Limón, Limón province, Costa Rica
cases.point: Siquirres, a town on the Route 32 corridor; the widening and the expropriations run the 107 km from the Route 4 junction to Limón (Nominatim for Siquirres; corridor endpoints from AidData record 37364)

lenders.name: China Eximbank
lenders.role: Two financing agreements signed with the Government of Costa Rica on 3 June 2013 for the rehabilitation and widening of National Route 32 between the Route 4 junction and Limón: a US$296 million buyer's credit, loan number 1420202052013211015, at 4% over 20 years with a 5-year grace period (AidData record 37364), and a government concessional loan of RMB 628 million at 2% over 20 years with a 5-year grace period (AidData record 39847). Costa Rica's Congress ratified both through Law 9293 (AidData).

cases.conditions: The two loans were to cover 85% of a US$465,593,387.06 engineering, procurement and construction contract, CONAVI-CHEC-00, between Costa Rica's National Road Council and China Harbour Engineering Company, signed the same day as the loans (AidData record 37364).

companies.name: China Harbour Engineering Company Ltd. (CHEC)
companies.role: Engineering, procurement and construction contractor, ordered to start work by CONAVI on 20 November 2017
companies.desc: Chinese contractor for ports, dredging, land reclamation, roads and railways, set up in 1980 and a subsidiary of China Communications Construction Company (CCCC).

companies.name: Consejo Nacional de Vialidad (CONAVI)
companies.role: Borrower's implementing body, responsible for the expropriations and for the contract with CHEC
companies.desc: The National Road Council, a body under Costa Rica's Ministry of Public Works and Transport that builds and maintains the national road network. Land files pass to the ministry's Real Estate Acquisition Directorate (DABI) for the expropriation itself.

cases.community: Finance minister Nogui Acosta told the Legislative Assembly's special Limón commission on 2 November 2023 that the works had been started without the expropriations ready, and listed that among the project's problems (Semanario Universidad). CONAVI's executive works report 48, cut off at September 2022, records 637 expropriations needed: 182 of the plots, 28.57%, were in the State's hands, and another 164 had been entered into possession voluntarily under agreements with their owners while the payment was being formalised (CRHoy). A report by the UN Office for Project Services cut off at 31 March 2025 records 515 expropriation files handled, 408 of them effective, meaning registered in the State's name or with effective entry into possession, 89 of those; 107 still in process, of which 67 had voluntary entries into possession that had not been made effective; and 475 plots available for the works, 92%, of which 19 were awaiting demolition (La Nación). Before the works began, La República reported about 1,400 properties needing expropriation and about 700 cases of people occupying the right of way, and that the State's valuation covers the land only, not the cost of moving a business, customers lost or other losses to the owner (lawyer Natiuska Traña of Pacheco Coto, La República, 20 November 2017).
cases.displaced_note: No document read counts people or households moved. The counts are of plots: 164 entered into possession while payment was being formalised at September 2022, and 67 at 31 March 2025.
cases.outcome: CHEC claimed US$25 million from CONAVI in 2022, saying right of way had not been handed over on time in some sections and citing cost increases from inflation; the public works minister said the country was not in a position to take on more cost (CRHoy). Design and construction ran at 71.65% against 89.33% planned at the end of September 2022 (CONAVI report 48, via CRHoy). The finance minister put the cost at US$552.5 million against US$485.6 million originally, with completion moved from September 2020 to December 2024 (Semanario Universidad). The head of the executing unit said in May 2025 that sections would be functional in October (La Nación).

A pocos meses de entregar la ruta 32, esto vuelve a complicar el proyecto
Ampliación de Ruta 32 estaría lista en diciembre de 2024 a un costo 14% mayor al monto original
Ampliación de Ruta 32 corre peligro por 1.400 expropiaciones

cases.confidence_note: The harm recorded is land put to work before payment was settled, counted in plots: 164 at September 2022 and 67 at 31 March 2025. The sources sit outside the lender: CONAVI's own works report and a UN Office for Project Services report, both reported by national newspapers, and a finance minister's statement to parliament. No document read names an owner left unpaid or records a sum owed. Three counts of the expropriations needed do not line up and the documents do not explain the gap: about 1,400 properties before the works started (La República, 2017), 637 required (CONAVI works report 48, September 2022) and 515 files handled (UN Office for Project Services, 31 March 2025).
cases.whole: The project widens 107 km of National Route 32 from two lanes to four between the Route 4 junction and Limón, the road that carries most of Costa Rica's foreign trade to the ports of Moín and Limón (AidData). The finance minister told the Legislative Assembly's Limón commission on 2 November 2023 that the cost had risen from US$485.6 million to US$552.5 million and completion had moved from September 2020 to December 2024 (Semanario Universidad). At 31 March 2025 the project had 475 plots available to work on, 92% of the expropriations, with 107 files still in process (UN Office for Project Services report, via La Nación).
